description:
Kernel auto-selection v2 is a serving-runtime performance project to ship improved kernel selection logic that chooses the best attention/matmul kernels based on (1) model family/architecture, (2) sequence-length regime (prefill vs decode; short vs long context buckets), and (3) GPU type/SKU (e.g., A10/L4/A100/H100, SM version, memory constraints). The goal is to improve p50/p95 latency and throughput stability across heterogeneous fleets and mixed customer workloads while reducing the incidence of kernel-related regressions when new models or GPUs are added.

Scope includes: defining a versioned kernel-selection policy, adding a model-family + GPU capability matrix, instrumenting decision telemetry (selected kernel, fallback reason, perf counters), integrating with scheduler signals (batch shape/seq length distribution) to avoid pathological choices, expanding microbench/perf-canary coverage for representative buckets, and establishing rollout guardrails (feature flag, canary, auto-disable on regression). Out of scope: writing entirely new kernel implementations (only wiring and selection changes), major scheduler rewrites unrelated to kernel selection, and customer-facing pricing/packaging changes.

Stakeholders: Serving Runtime (Kernel team led by Hiro Tanaka; Scheduling team led by Sofia Ivanova; runtime architecture led by Noah Patel), SRE/Observability (Sean Gallagher org) for rollout safety and regression monitoring, Infra/Fleet (Irene Choi org) for GPU SKU mapping and capability detection, and Release Engineering (Connor O’Brien) for release train gating and backout procedures. Product is informed for customer-impact prioritization and release notes.

Proposed timeline (8 weeks):
1) Weeks 1–2: design + ADRs, define buckets and policy; confirm GPU/model taxonomy.
2) Weeks 2–5: implementation behind a feature flag; add telemetry; add/adjust tests.
3) Weeks 4–6: benchmark suite + perf-canary expansion; validate on staging across GPUs.
4) Weeks 6–7: production canary (1–5% traffic) with automated rollback thresholds.
5) Week 8: ramp to 100%, finalize docs/runbooks, and publish post-launch perf analysis.

Key constraints: correctness first (no numerical drift beyond tolerance), deterministic selection for reproducibility, low runtime overhead for decision logic, and safe fallback behavior for unknown model families or GPUs. Deliverables: v2 selector code path, configuration/registry entries, dashboards/alerts, updated runbooks, release notes, and a short post-launch report comparing baseline vs v2 across key buckets.

files.description: Primary design doc: problem statement, current v1 behavior, proposed v2 policy keyed on model family/seq length/GPU type, bucket definitions, fallback rules, config/registry format, and success metrics.

ADR documenting why the selector keys on (model family, seq length buckets, GPU capability) and explicitly not on request-level features that would add overhead/instability; includes alternatives considered.
ADR for rollout safety: feature flag strategy, canary ramp, auto-disable thresholds (p95 latency, error rate, OOM), and ownership/oncall procedures.
Benchmark plan: representative model families, seq length buckets, GPU SKUs, batch shapes; how to run locally/CI; how results are stored and compared.
Operational runbook for canarying and ramping v2, including dashboards to watch, rollback steps, and how to interpret selector telemetry and fallback reasons.
Standard for required runtime telemetry fields (selected kernel, candidate set, rejection/fallback reasons, GPU capability snapshot) and cardinality guidance.
Release notes entry: what changed, expected perf impact by bucket, known caveats, and how to disable/override selection if needed.
Working notes doc: open questions, quick experiments, links to PRs/bench runs, and draft bucket boundaries before being finalized in Confluence.
Spreadsheet-style table mapping GPU SKUs to capabilities (SM version, shared memory limits, preferred kernels, known hazards) used by the selector.
Draft taxonomy of model families/architectures and the runtime signals used to classify them; includes edge cases for new/rare architectures.
SRE-focused doc collecting canary metrics links, initial thresholds, and notes from dry runs in staging.
Launch checklist: gating criteria, sign-offs, comms plan, and backout steps aligned to the release train.
Project umbrella ticket: 'Kernel auto-selection v2 implementation' with goals, non-goals, milestones, and links to design docs and dashboards.
Implement v2 selector interface + versioning (v1/v2 coexistence) behind feature flag; acceptance criteria includes deterministic selection and low overhead.
Define seq length buckets and batch-shape signals (prefill/decode split, context length thresholds) and validate against real traffic distributions.
Add model-family classification in runtime (metadata registry + fallback) with tests for common model architectures.
GPU capability detection and SKU mapping: plumb SM version/memory features into runtime; dependency on Infra for canonical SKU names.
Selector decision telemetry: emit selected kernel + candidate/fallback reason; include sampling strategy and cardinality constraints.
Perf suite expansion: add benchmark cases for long-context buckets on H100/A100 and small-batch low-latency on L4/A10.
Integrate perf-canary gating for selector regressions; define pass/fail thresholds and reporting format for release train.
Implement automatic rollback/auto-disable: wire SRE thresholds (latency/error/OOM) to flip flag and page oncall.
Staging soak + correctness validation: numerical tolerance checks, rare architecture tests, and mixed-workload stress.
Production canary and ramp plan issue with task checklist (1% → 5% → 25% → 100%) and required sign-offs.
Post-launch analysis ticket: compare v1 vs v2 by bucket, summarize wins/regressions, and create follow-up backlog items.
PR: introduce kernel selector v2 scaffold, feature flag plumbing, and config loading; includes unit tests and CI wiring.
PR: add model-family classifier (llama/mistral/qwen/etc.) with registry entries and fallback behavior for unknown families.
PR: implement seq length bucketization and prefill/decode shape extraction; adds tests for boundary conditions.
PR: plumb GPU capability snapshot (SM version, shared memory class, fp8 support flag) into runtime context for selection.
PR: implement initial selection policy for A100/H100 across short/medium/long context buckets; includes fallback reasons.
PR: tune selection for L4/A10 low-latency buckets; addresses small-batch decode tail latency.
PR: add structured telemetry fields for selector decisions, sampling, and log/metric emission guidelines.
PR: harden fallback behavior when GPU SKU is unknown/misreported; ensures safe default kernel and emits diagnostic counters.
PR: add correctness/conformance tests to prevent numerical drift and catch architecture-specific failures.
PR: add perf regression guardrails (assertions/threshold checks in perf test harness) focused on long-context prefill.
PR: define versioned config schema for kernel selection policy; includes migration notes and validation.
PR: integrate scheduler signals (batch composition, queue depth) to avoid pathological kernel choices under mixed load.
PR: add runtime hook to allow control-plane to auto-disable selector v2 based on regression signals.
PR: add internal release notes stub + links to Confluence pages and runbook references.
PR: add benchmark cases for long-context buckets and model-family sweep; stores results in standardized output format.
PR: add pipeline to import GPU SKU capability matrix from a canonical table for benchmark labeling.
PR: add perf-canary job for kernel selector v2, including threshold checks and Slack notification integration.
PR: report perf metrics bucketed by seq length + GPU type; generates diff against baseline and links to dashboards.
PR: add dashboard panels for selected kernel rates, fallback reasons, and latency deltas by bucket; includes alert suggestions.
PR: add alert for spikes in fallback reasons (unknown GPU/model family) as early warning of misconfig or new SKU rollout.
PR: internal docs update describing how to interpret selector telemetry and how to override/disable in emergencies.
Thread: runtime engineers coordinating the initial v2 selector scaffold, agreeing on config shape and feature flag naming.
Thread: debugging a staging regression where long-context prefill selects an unexpected kernel; includes logs and quick patch discussion.
Thread: discussion on seq length bucket boundaries using production histograms; includes proposed thresholds and follow-ups.
Thread: design review Q&A about selector inputs, determinism, and how to prevent per-request variability; links to ADR drafts.
Thread: infra + runtime align on canonical GPU SKU naming and capability detection (SM versions, MIG quirks).
Thread: SRE proposes canary ramp + rollback thresholds; discussion of which metrics are reliable for fast rollback.
Thread: release engineering coordinating inclusion of KASv2 in runtime-1.19; checklists, gating, and who signs off.
Thread: incident triage for elevated latency on a subset of H100 nodes during canary; includes mitigations and decision to pause ramp.
Thread: post-incident follow-up discussing root cause hypothesis (fallback spike due to unknown SKU) and action items to harden detection.
Support ticket: enterprise customer reports p95 latency regression on long-context prompts on H100; investigation links to selector behavior and canary metrics.
Support ticket: dedicated customer sees intermittent OOMs after runtime update; suspected kernel mismatch for specific model family; includes workaround and follow-up PR references.
Internal ticket: CI GPU runners flaky after adding new microbench suite; request for test runtime limits and retry strategy.
Technical deep dive transcript with prospect/customer 'Northstar AI' focused on long-context latency; requests clearer behavior across GPU SKUs and model families.
HubSpot company record for Northstar AI: requirements around long-context workloads, GPU preferences, evaluation status, and linked deep-dive meeting/support items.

Email thread: release approval and risk sign-off for including KASv2 in runtime-1.19; includes rollout plan, gating results, and backout owners (internal participants limited to gmail-exported leaders/managers).
